newsitem.title: HONG KONG: State Street Bank eyes China fund market.
newsitem.headline: State Street Bank eyes China fund market.

text.p: State Street Bank is teaming up with a local Hong Kong brokerage and investment firm to tap into China's potentially huge number of mutual fund investors.

"We would eventually like to tap into the mutual fund market in China, but we are also looking for this joint venture to provide opportunities for direct investments in China," said Ralph Constantino, managing director at State Street Global Advisors, the investment management group of State Street.

State Street Bank and Mansion House Group of Hong Kong have formed as equal partners a joint venture company to provide asset management and mutual fund services relating to Hong Kong, China and the region.
State Street Bank is the principal subsidiary of State Street Corp of the United States. Mansion House is active in stock brokerage, asset management and direct investment in China.
China has a population of 1.2 billion people that eventually must put away money for retirement. And as in many Asian nations, China has a high savings rate.
State Street would like to tap into those savings, Constantino said.
Nicholas Lopardo, chairman and chief executive officer of State Street Global Advisors, is chairman of the new firm.
Evans Lowe, chairman and chief executive officer of Mansion House, is vice chairman.
"The JV (joint venture) is a logical extension of what we've been doing all along in other countries in that we try to match a local solution to local needs," said Constantino
"We don't export what we have in the U.S. to other countries because every country has country-specific legal issues and investor preferences," he said.
State Street has about US$360 billion under management, mostly in the form of institutional money. Just a tiny portion of that represents the savings of Asian investors.
In forming a venture with Mansion House, which already has investments, both direct and indirect in China, State Street hopes to make inroads in the mainland market.

"We think a lot of people will be approaching China with their standard products. But having a Hong Kong partner with strong ties to the mainland, we hope to offer something different," Constantino said.
